newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks led up by conglomerate flagships.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks led up by conglomerate flagships.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 3 Reuter - Colombian stocks edged up again Thursday as demand for top conglomerates continued.
Bogota's IBB index rose 0.32 percent to 1,080.1 on volume of 6.3 billion pesos, while Medellin's IBOMED index gained a paper-thin 0.06 percent to end at 16,673.66 amid a six billion peso trade.
"There area lot of foreign buyers, while local investors are holding off because they're a little more speculative and are waiting for prices to drop," one Bogota trader said.
"The falls on Wall Street and hopes for a low inflation rate have also had an effect."
The bulk of the volume in Medellin was made up of chocolate maker Nacional de Chocolates, part of the Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate.
Over 2.8 billion pesos of the stock changed hands in eight cross deals, dropping 1.05 percent to 9,400.1.
Demand for brewing giant Bavaria remained high. It gained 1.67 percent in Bogota to reach a new high of 7,300 and was up 1.68 percent at 7,320 in Medellin.
Cement maker Cemento Argos, head of the cement producing arm of the Sindicato Antioqueno, remained unchanged in Medellin and Bogota at 7,850 amid heavy demand.
Banco Bancoquia, the financial powerhouse of the Santo Domingo business empire, rose 2.5 percent to 3,321 in Bogota, but dipped 0.9 percent to 3,320 in Medellin.
